# Belinda

## Overview

- **Age:** 14 years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P38](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0038), [v2 c21 P51](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0051)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P38](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0038)</sub>
- **Role:** Domestic maid for Rosalind Penrose  <sub>[v2 c21 P38](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0038)</sub>
- **Titles:** Belinda the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P38](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0038), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Appearance

Belinda is a small girl with a freckled face, a snub nose, and a wide mouth that stretches from ear to ear. She has long fair hair worn in two heavy braids fastened with oversized blue ribbon bows. On special occasions, she wears heavily starched white dresses and dramatic ribbon bows that resemble cherub wings.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P38](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0038), [v2 c30 P27](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0027), [v2 c30 P28](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0028)_

## Personality

Belinda is industrious, pragmatic, and fiercely devoted to her mistress, Rosalind Penrose. Though straightforward and matter-of-fact in her worldview, she indulges her mistress's playful imaginative games without complaint. She holds strong, cynical opinions about men and marriage, yet she deeply desires Rosalind's happiness. She admires Nell Harcourt and continuously tries to copy her graceful manners.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P65](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0065), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c28 P15](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0015), [v2 c28 P28](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0028), [v2 c30 P28](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0028)_

## Goals

- To care faithfully for Miss Rosalind  <sub>[v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c28 P15](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0015)</sub>
- To learn to walk and carry herself gracefully like Nell Harcourt  <sub>[v2 c27 P49](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0049), [v2 c30 P28](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0028)</sub>

## History

Belinda came to reside at Echo Cottage to serve as maid for Rosalind Penrose, following three of her elder sisters who had previously filled the same role. Because Rosalind continually called her predecessor by the name Belinda, she adopted the designation 'Belinda the Fourth'. She dutifully managed domestic tasks and indulged Rosalind's pretend tea parties and imaginative games. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke stumbled upon Echo Cottage, Belinda welcomed them warmly and struck up a close friendship with Nell, whom she tried to imitate. When Stephen Stanhope returned to woo Rosalind, Belinda excitedly followed the romance and cheered for their union. On the day of Rosalind and Stephen's wedding at Echo Cottage, she assisted with preparations and threw a shoe for good luck that struck the minister. Following the wedding, she prepared to accompany the newlyweds to live with them in Boston.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P38](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0038), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P49](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0049), [v2 c28 P15](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0015), [v2 c28 P71](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0071), [v2 c29 P3](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0003), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011), [v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033)_

## Background by volume

- Actual name is Leonora Bowman  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Fourth daughter in the Bowman family to work as Miss Rosalind's maid  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Came to reside at Echo Cottage at age thirteen in exchange for room, board, and garments  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Has a married sister who was wedded three times  <sub>[v2 c28 P15](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0015)</sub>

> There is nothing I can do, and remaining here merely waiting is terrible. What if he fails to propose in the end, Miss Harcourt, ma’am? One can never feel certain about those men.  <sub>[v2 c28 P15](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0015)</sub>

> When everything is finished, Miss Harcourt, ma'am, a wedding isn't really much happier than a funeral.  <sub>[v2 c30 P35](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0035)</sub>
